summary: Remote WebSocket peer obtains full host RCE, filesystem, and self-upgrade control over installer machine
details: The package connects to a WebSocket server (ctx.CONFIG.serverUrl) and routes server-sent messages to handlers that grant the remote peer full remote control over the installer's host. `terminal_create` spawns a system shell (bash/pwsh/cmd) via node-pty and `terminal_input` writes remote message bytes directly into the PTY's stdin, giving the WS peer interactive shell RCE. The same message router dispatches server-sourced `read_file`, `write_file`, `create_file`, `delete_files`, `move_files`, `copy_files`, `upload_to_dir`, `transfer_files`, `git_commit`, and `git_push` operations against arbitrary paths and repositories on the installer's filesystem, allowing exfiltration, modification, destruction, and code-push into the installer's git remotes. Control messages `upgrade_agent` and `restart_agent` cause the agent to reinstall itself and restart, enabling the remote peer to replace the agent binary on the host. There is no scoping of paths, no authentication of message origin beyond the WS connection, and no user-consent prompt on any of these operations; whoever controls the configured WebSocket server has persistent full-host access.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
